intended_object: A helper isomorphism `shiftFunctor C a ⋙ F ≅ F ⋙ shiftFunctor D a`. It is built from `e : F ⋙ G ≅ H`, the shift isomorphisms of `G` and `H`, and full faithfulness of `G`. The docstring says it exists only to build `Functor.CommShift.ofComp`.
explanation: The docstring calls this an "Auxiliary definition for `Functor.CommShift.ofComp`", and it sits in the helper namespace `OfComp`. It is one step of a construction: it supplies the component isomorphisms that are later bundled into a `CommShift` instance on `F`. It is not a notion from the literature in its own right. Its body is consistent with that role. It starts from the composite isomorphism (shift ⋙ F) ⋙ G ≅ (F ⋙ shift) ⋙ G, which is built from `e`, `H.commShiftIso a` and the inverse of `G.commShiftIso a`. Since `G` is fully faithful, whiskering on the right by `G` is fully faithful too, so the composite can be pulled back through it with `preimageIso`. This is an implementation step, so the verdict is not_a_mathematical_object.
